children: The big win for the Democrats in midterm elections presents contrasting reflections on the direction the party may take ahead, Commerzbank's Christoph Balz says in a note. The left wing of the party, including the Democratic Socialists of America, likely feel vindicated as a number of its representatives were elected. "On the other hand, moderate Democrats achieved spectacular successes on what is typically Republican terrain," he says. In some states, such as Texas, Ohio and Georgia, where data-center expansion is being promoted, Republican governors were voted out of office. But an argument against a clear shift to the left comes as proposals for a wealth tax for billionaires in California looks set to be rejected, he says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)
